home_faq_agents_a: Claude Code, Codex and omp on your computer, and OpenCode too on a crew server. {#code}atlas setup{/code} finds them, shows what it would change and connects Atlas to each one. Other agents that speak MCP can be connected by hand.
home_faq_agents_q: Which agents does it work with?
home_faq_compare_a: Those start processes. Atlas also gives agents a place to work (a worktree each, a crew on your server, approvals) and the live project through MCP. The README's comparison is honest about where the others win.
home_faq_compare_q: How is it different from process-compose, mprocs or Tilt?
home_faq_cost_a: Nothing. Atlas is free and open source, MIT or Apache-2.0. Agents run on your own subscription or API key with their provider; Atlas never charges for or resells model use.
home_faq_install_a: Get it from the {#link}download page{/link}: the app for {mac}, {windows} and Linux, each with the command-line tool. From a terminal: {#code}curl -fsSL https://atlas.codeatlas.com.br/install.sh | sh{/code} ({mac} and Linux) or {#code}irm https://atlas.codeatlas.com.br/install.ps1 | iex{/code} (PowerShell). Both check the download's SHA-256.
home_faq_join_fine: Open source, MIT or Apache-2.0, for {platforms} ({#link}all downloads{/link}). More processor types are coming; until then you can {#link2}compile it from source{/link2}.
home_faq_notes_fine: One email per release, nothing else. Or follow {#link}the repository on GitHub{/link}.
home_faq_privacy_a: No. Atlas is local first, with no account and no telemetry. Logs stay in {#code}.logs/{/code} in your project, and the app only contacts GitHub to check for updates. A crew runs on a server you own. If you pair a phone, a notification carries only the kind of event, the agent and the folder name, never your code or prompts.
home_faq_privacy_q: Does it send my code or logs anywhere?
home_faq_quit_a: No. Terminals, projects and agents live in a background service, so they keep running when the app quits, crashes or updates.
home_faq_quit_q: Does closing the app stop my work?
home_faq_signed_a: On {mac}, yes: every release is signed and notarized by Apple. On {windows}, not yet: {#code}Atlas-Setup.exe{/code} is made by GitHub Actions from the release tag and has a published SHA-256, but no signature, so SmartScreen may warn. Choose More info, then Run anyway. Signing through the SignPath Foundation is pending.
home_faq_what_a: A free, open-source workspace where AI agents do real work on your projects, each in its own space, while a person stays responsible for what ships.
home_faq_what_q: What is Atlas, in one sentence?
home_faq_who_a: Today, mostly yes: Atlas runs projects and coding agents, and a crew server takes a Linux machine you reach over SSH. Grand Line is about bringing the same model to the rest of a company, and this page will say when that is real.
home_faq_who_q: Do I need to be a developer?
